title: Introduce circuit-conciliator and soft-shed ETA harmonizer to reduce oscillations during regional failovers
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds a new circuit conciliator service to coordinate circuit state across regions and a soft-shed ETA harmonizer that smooths load-shedding decisions to avoid rapid oscillation. Improves regional failover stability and reduces customer-visible SLO blips under transient overloads.
description: Context and motivation: We observed repeated oscillation in tenant-level circuit states during regional egress spikes: regional circuits would open/close rapidly, causing cascading failovers and repeated SLO blips across tenants. This is most visible for tenants with bursty traffic spanning multiple regions (see ENG-1482). The change: Introduce two cooperating components: 1) circuit-conciliator (a lightweight cross-region reconciler) that maintains a small consistent view of circuit buckets and enforces a damped decision window so circuits do not flip faster than a tuned hysteresis period; 2) soft-shed ETA harmonizer which augments load-shedding percentages with an estimated time-to-clear (ETA) signal derived from queue backlog and recent processing rate. Together they produce a gradual, probabilistic soft-shed that ramps down traffic instead of immediate binary circuit transitions. Implementation notes: - circuit-conciliator runs as part of the runtime control-plane. It exposes a reconciliation API and a local policy engine that prefers the highest-safety (more-shed) state but will respect a short keepalive to avoid re-opening until ETA improves. - ETA harmonizer computes a per-slot ETA using exponential smoothing over backlog and tokens/sec and exposes a confidence score used to modulate shed strength. - We added a compact protobuf for cross-region conciliator messages and a small persistence layer to retain transient circuit epochs for up to the configured hysteresis window. - Default tuning is conservative off-by-default for Dedicated customers; hosted rollout will be gradual and behind a feature flag. Risks and mitigations: - New cross-region messages increase control-plane chatter: we limit fanout to bucket-summary deltas and compress updates. - Mis-tuning could over-shed traffic; we ship with telemetry (see metrics/conciliator_* and harmonizer_*), end-to-end e2e test coverage, and a rollback toggle in the config. The description below includes a small illustrative snippet (not the full diff) to show the reconciliation loop logic. Reconciliation snippet: "for each bucket: if remote_state.consensus_shed > local_shed and time_since_change > min_hysteresis: adopt remote_shed else keep local with decay" Related work items: ENG-1482 (investigation), ENG-1501 (SLO-stability epic), SUP-4321 (customer incident that triggered hotfix).

c3d01aa perf: tighten default hysteresis and add integration tests; telemetry and docs
review_comments: Luca Fernandez (reviewer): Nice approach. Two questions: 1) can you clarify how the conciliator chooses tie-breaks when regions disagree? 2) we should ensure the persistence window doesn't exceed our leader-election TTLs.

Asha Menon (author): Tie-breaks favor the more-conservative state (higher shed). The proto includes an epoch counter; conciliator picks higher epoch unless both epochs are within hysteresis window, then picks conservative. Persistence window default set to 120s and is bounded by leader-election TTL - documented in defaults.yaml.
Maya Patel (reviewer): Integration tests look good. One nit: can we add a small e2e test covering an alternating spike pattern (region A spike then region B) to validate no reopen flip-flopping?

Asha Menon (author): Added tests/integration/test_conciliator_end_to_end.py which simulates alternating spikes and asserts at-most-one state transition per hysteresis window. Also added bench to reproduce scenario.

Evan Leung (approver): Verified on staging. Observed 3x reduction in reopen frequency during simulated cross-region bursts. CI perf bench had a flaky test that I reran; passing now. Approving for merge.
Security (comment): throttling decisions use bucket ids only; no tenant PII is transmitted. Confirmed encryption is applied for control-plane proto in transit.
QA (comment): added two minor test failures that were fixed in commit c3d01aa; all passing now.
